narrativeReportMd:
# MedicinalProductIngredient R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` is not present as an R6 resource. The likely successor is R6 `Ingredient`, but it is not a pure rename: the resource identity, required status, manufacturer representation, substance/CodeableReference model, specified-substance branch, and strength representation all changed in locally breaking ways.

## Scope
This report compares the R4 StructureDefinition for `MedicinalProductIngredient` with the R6 `Ingredient` StructureDefinition because the assigned R6 path is absent and R6 marks `MedicinalProductIngredient` as an old type. Inherited base-resource changes are excluded.

## Main migration themes
Existing R4 instances cannot be made R6-valid by only changing `resourceType`. A migration must add `Ingredient.status`, reshape manufacturer references, map or split `specifiedSubstance`, put substance codes into `CodeableReference.concept` or references to `SubstanceDefinition`, and rewrite strength fields to R6 choice-element names such as `presentationRatio` or `presentationRatioRange`.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are the artifact replacement itself, the added required modifier status, the manufacturer backbone conversion, the mandatory substance/CodeableReference conversion, collapse of `specifiedSubstance`, and the strength/reference-strength remodeling.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most important for deciding whether repeated R4 `specifiedSubstance` entries become multiple R6 `Ingredient` resources, how to preserve R4 confidentiality, and whether text or extensions are needed when R6 strength choices cannot be represented in R4.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Several goals could have been achieved with less R4-to-R6 disruption by retaining aliases, deprecated elements, or additive choices. The current R6 model is cleaner and more expressive but requires explicit transforms.

## Follow-up analysis
Review `SubstanceDefinition`, terminology expansions, and any official cross-version mapping when available before implementing production migration.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` is locally replaced/remodeled as R6 `Ingredient`; hard migration issues include resource identity, required modifier `status`, manufacturer wrapping, mandatory `substance`, `CodeableReference`, removal/collapse of `specifiedSubstance`, and strength choice remodeling. The main uncertainty is the absence of an official cross-version ConceptMap.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is a structural transform, not a version-label update. Systems must instantiate R6 `Ingredient`, add a lifecycle `status`, move R4 `manufacturer` references under `manufacturer.manufacturer`, convert R4 CodeableConcept substance fields into R6 CodeableReference concepts or references, and rewrite strength fields to R6 choice properties. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy for R6-only fields such as `for`, `function`, manufacturer role, non-Ratio strengths, SubstanceDefinition references, and text strengths.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for computable structural differences because they are directly visible in the local StructureDefinitions and package index. Confidence is medium for exact business-intent mapping from R4 `specifiedSubstance` to R6 `Ingredient.substance` because no official diff, narrative rationale, or ConceptMap was available.

findings.title: R4 MedicinalProductIngredient is absent in R6 and appears replaced by Ingredient

oldState.summary: R4 has a concrete resource type `MedicinalProductIngredient`.
oldState.narrativeMd: The R4 core package includes `StructureDefinition-MedicinalProductIngredient.json` with canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/MedicinalProductIngredient`, type `MedicinalProductIngredient`, and draft status.

newState.summary: R6 has no `MedicinalProductIngredient` StructureDefinition; `Ingredient` is the likely successor.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 package has `StructureDefinition-Ingredient.json` with the same high-level description. The R6 `fhir-old-types` CodeSystem lists `MedicinalProductIngredient` as an old resource name.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 resource name is shorter but has the same description and category, and the R6 package explicitly lists the old R4 name as an old type.

impact.impactRationaleMd: FHIR resource identity is part of the wire format. An R4 instance with `resourceType: "MedicinalProductIngredient"` will not validate as an R6 core resource, and R6 `Ingredient` instances will not be accepted by strict R4 parsers expecting the old resource type.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Medication-definition systems that route, authorize, or validate by resource type can silently drop or reject ingredient records unless the replacement is explicitly mapped.

justification.inferredGoal: Rename and remodel the medication-definition ingredient resource into the R6 `Ingredient` model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` resource name/canonical in base R6 while improving definitions, aliases, and child content as needed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 successor has the same high-level description and R6 explicitly marks `MedicinalProductIngredient` as an old type, so the replacement appears intentional. The local evidence does not show that shortening the resource name to `Ingredient` was necessary enough to justify making every R4 instance fail at the resourceType/canonical level before element migration even starts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have kept `MedicinalProductIngredient` as the canonical resource type and used title, aliases, descriptions, and profile guidance to communicate the broader or cleaner R6 model. That would preserve R4 parser and endpoint compatibility for the resource identity. Adding both `MedicinalProductIngredient` and `Ingredient` as parallel core resources would have a larger duplication risk, but simply retaining the old name while evolving the content is a plausible low-to-moderate tradeoff.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Keeps a longer medicinal-product-specific name, but avoids a wire-format resourceType break without creating duplicate resource names.

evidence.detail: R4 defines a concrete `MedicinalProductIngredient` resource.
R6 defines a concrete `Ingredient` resource with the same high-level description.
R6 old-type terminology includes `MedicinalProductIngredient`.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are minimal fragments showing the resource-type identity break, not complete production records.

findings.narrativeMd: The assigned resource no longer exists under its R4 name in R6. Even before considering child elements, strict FHIR serializers, validators, generated models, REST endpoints, search routing, and resource-type switches must be updated from `MedicinalProductIngredient` to `Ingredient`.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance with the old `resourceType` is old-valid/new-invalid in R6. Conversely, an R6 `Ingredient` resource is not a recognized R4 resource type. This affects validation, REST type URLs, Bundle entries, resource-specific search parameters, and generated class names.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit resource-type transform from `MedicinalProductIngredient` to `Ingredient` and then apply the element-level transforms described in the other findings. Test Bundle migration, REST route generation, type discriminator handling, and parser registration.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The observed replacement could have been less disruptive if R6 retained a deprecated resource definition or supplied an official ConceptMap. Without that, every implementation must carry its own compatibility mapping.

findings.title: R6 Ingredient adds required modifier `status` with required publication-status binding

oldState.summary: No equivalent local status element exists on R4 MedicinalProductIngredient.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` has no lifecycle/status field in its local element list.

newState.summary: `Ingredient.status` is mandatory, isModifier=true, and is bound to publication-status.

flags.isModifierReason: This is labeled as "Is Modifier" because applications should not use a retired {{title}} without due consideration

semanticText.definition: The status of this ingredient. Enables tracking the life-cycle of the content.
semanticText.comment: Allows filtering of ingredient that are appropriate for use versus not.

newState.narrativeMd: Every R6 `Ingredient` must state a publication status such as `active`, and consumers must treat retired content differently because the element is a modifier.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct validation break after resource-type migration: an R4 instance has no `status`, while R6 requires exactly one status code from a required value set. The modifier flag also creates runtime risk for clients that ignore modifier elements.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Using a retired ingredient as if active can affect regulatory or product-definition decisions.

justification.inferredGoal: Add lifecycle governance to the ingredient resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make `status` optional in the base resource, with a best-practice invariant or stricter profiles requiring it where lifecycle governance is needed.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: A lifecycle status is a reasonable R6 goal for definitional medication content, and making it a modifier ensures consumers consider retired or unknown content. The break is still real because R4 has no local status value to migrate mechanically. The less-breaking alternative is incomplete because it would allow base R6 Ingredient records with no lifecycle state.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base `0..1` `status`, optionally paired with a warning or best-practice invariant, would keep R4-origin records base-valid while still enabling systems that know the lifecycle state to populate it. Profiles for regulated publication workflows could require `status`. This is only a partial alternative because consumers would lose the uniform R6 guarantee that every base Ingredient declares whether it is active, retired, draft, or unknown.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old data but weakens the base guarantee that all ingredients can be filtered by active/retired lifecycle status.

evidence.detail: No `MedicinalProductIngredient.status` element is present.
R6 `Ingredient.status` has cardinality 1..1, type code, required publication-status binding, and isModifier=true.

examples.examplesMd: The old-valid/new-invalid fragment assumes the resourceType has already been renamed during migration; it demonstrates omission of required R6 `status`.

findings.narrativeMd: `Ingredient.status` is new, mandatory, and modifier. R4 data has no field from which a lifecycle state can be mechanically inferred in all cases, so migrations must choose a default policy or source status from external business metadata.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: After mapping the resource name, any migrated R6 `Ingredient` without `status` fails cardinality validation. If `status` is present but outside the publication-status value set, it fails required-binding validation. Runtime consumers must not ignore this modifier because `retired` changes whether the ingredient should be used.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define a status mapping policy. Common choices are `active` for current production content, `retired` for discontinued ingredient definitions, or `unknown` when source governance is unavailable. Test validation for omitted, invalid-code, active, retired, and unknown statuses.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Making status mandatory is useful but avoidable as a base breaking change. A profile-level requirement or best-practice invariant would have allowed old data to remain base-valid while still supporting stricter regulated workflows.

findings.title: `manufacturer` changes from direct Organization Reference to a backbone with manufacturer role

oldState.narrativeMd: Each R4 manufacturer repetition is itself a Reference to an Organization.

newState.summary: R6 `manufacturer` is 0..* BackboneElement with required child `manufacturer.manufacturer` Reference(Organization) and optional coded `manufacturer.role`.
newState.narrativeMd: The Organization reference moved under `Ingredient.manufacturer.manufacturer`; `Ingredient.manufacturer.role` can classify the organization as `allowed`, `possible`, or `actual`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The names and definitions match the manufacturer concept, but R6 wraps the reference to add association-role metadata.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance that has `manufacturer` as a direct Reference will serialize the wrong shape for R6. Generated classes also change from `Reference[]` to a backbone array. R6 manufacturer roles have no R4 destination except extension or profile-specific loss.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing whether a manufacturer is actual, possible, or merely allowed can change regulatory interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow richer manufacturer association details without repeating separate extensions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `manufacturer` as `Reference(Organization)` and add optional base association-role metadata by a separate keyed/backbone element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 backbone cleanly attaches role metadata to each manufacturer association, which is a reasonable modeling improvement. A less-breaking design could preserve the direct reference shape, but doing so would make it harder to express whether each organization is actual, possible, or allowed without ambiguous parallel arrays or duplicate association structures.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `manufacturer` as the repeating Organization reference and introduced an optional `manufacturerAssociation` or keyed role element that points at a manufacturer reference. That would preserve R4 wire shape for common data. It is only a partial alternative because the added role must stay synchronized with the referenced organization; duplicate direct-reference and association forms could persist indefinitely and produce validation or interpretation ambiguity.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoids breaking existing reference arrays but creates alignment and duplication risks between manufacturer references and role metadata.

evidence.detail: R4 manufacturer is 0..* Reference targeting Organization.
R6 manufacturer is 0..* BackboneElement.
The R6 Organization reference is the required child `manufacturer.manufacturer`.

examples.examplesMd: The old-valid/new-invalid fragment uses the R4 direct-reference shape at the R6 path to show why a wrapper transform is required.

findings.narrativeMd: The manufacturer association is not just renamed; its JSON shape and generated type change. R4 code that expects `manufacturer[n].reference` must now read `manufacturer[n].manufacturer.reference`, and R6 may carry an association role that R4 cannot store natively.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 manufacturer content becomes invalid in R6 unless each Reference is wrapped in a backbone item. R6-to-R4 conversion can preserve the Organization reference but loses `manufacturer.role` unless an extension is used.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map each R4 `manufacturer` Reference to a new R6 `manufacturer` backbone with child `manufacturer`. If the source system knows whether the organization is `actual`, `possible`, or `allowed`, populate `manufacturer.role`; otherwise omit it rather than inventing a required-binding code.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The richer R6 model is understandable, but a sibling optional role element or extension would have been less disruptive for existing JSON and generated clients.

findings.title: `substance` becomes mandatory and its code changes from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference

oldState.summary: R4 `substance` is optional; `substance.code` is mandatory only if the optional backbone is present and is a CodeableConcept.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed an ingredient to omit `substance` and instead use `specifiedSubstance`, or omit both if constrained elsewhere.

newState.summary: R6 `substance` is 1..1; `substance.code` is 1..1 CodeableReference targeting SubstanceDefinition.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires a substance backbone and lets the substance be represented by either a concept or a reference to `SubstanceDefinition` through CodeableReference.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R4 `substance.code` and R6 `Ingredient.substance.code` carry the same high-level substance concept, but the R6 type is a different datatype and serialization shape.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances that do not populate `substance` can be invalid in R6. R4 instances that do populate `substance.code` still require a datatype transform because a CodeableConcept is not serialized the same way as CodeableReference. R6 references to `SubstanceDefinition` have no direct R4 equivalent.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The substance identity is clinically and regulatorily central; incorrect mapping can change what ingredient is represented.

justification.inferredGoal: Make the ingredient substance explicit and allow either coded or full SubstanceDefinition representation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `substance` optional and preserve `substance.code` as CodeableConcept while adding an optional SubstanceDefinition reference or separate richer identity field.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Making the ingredient substance explicit and linkable to `SubstanceDefinition` is domain-plausible, especially because substance identity is central to the resource. The base break is significant, but the best less-breaking design would not fully meet the R6 goal of a mandatory, single substance identity and would carry duplicate code/reference patterns.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have left `substance` at `0..1`, kept the existing `CodeableConcept` serialization at `substance.code`, and added an optional `substance.definition` reference for richer SubstanceDefinition linkage. That preserves R4 coded substances and instances relying on other branches. It is partial because base R6 would still allow ingredients without a substance and would need rules for reconciling coded and referenced substance identities.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves many R4 instances but permits incomplete ingredients and creates parallel code/reference representations.

evidence.detail: R4 `substance` has cardinality 0..1.
R4 `substance.code` is 1..1 CodeableConcept when `substance` exists.
R6 `substance` has cardinality 1..1.
R6 `substance.code` is CodeableReference targeting SubstanceDefinition.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows the typical CodeableConcept-to-CodeableReference.concept transform.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 centers the resource on a mandatory substance. Old data that relied on `specifiedSubstance` or lacked the simpler `substance` branch needs a mapping decision. Even when R4 has a CodeableConcept, it must be nested under `CodeableReference.concept` in R6.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-derived R6 instance without `Ingredient.substance` fails cardinality validation. An R4 CodeableConcept copied directly to `Ingredient.substance.code` fails datatype validation because R6 expects CodeableReference children. R6 reference-only substance identity cannot round-trip to R4 without dereferencing, coding, or extension.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Populate `Ingredient.substance.code.concept` from R4 `substance.code` when only coded data exists. Use `Ingredient.substance.code.reference` only when a corresponding `SubstanceDefinition` resource is available and the allergen invariant is satisfied. Audit R4 instances that use only `specifiedSubstance` because they need separate mapping.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 type is more expressive but could have preserved the R4 CodeableConcept shape by adding an optional reference sibling. The current CodeableReference design is compact but requires datatype-aware transforms and code-generation changes.

findings.title: R4 `specifiedSubstance` branch is removed/collapsed, with unclear handling for repeated specified substances and confidentiality

oldState.summary: R4 has 0..* `specifiedSubstance` entries with mandatory `code` and `group`, optional `confidentiality`, and nested strengths.
oldState.narrativeMd: `specifiedSubstance` could repeat. Each repetition had its own `code`, required specified-substance `group`, optional `confidentiality`, and strength information.

newState.summary: R6 has a single mandatory `substance`; `specifiedSubstance`, its `confidentiality`, and its required IDMP-like `group` path are not present.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 has `Ingredient.group` 0..1, but its definition is a physical-use classification, not the same computable element as R4 `specifiedSubstance.group`. No local R6 element directly carries R4 `specifiedSubstance.confidentiality`.

facts.newValue: No direct equivalent; Ingredient.group 0..1 has different definition
No direct local R6 element found

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: R6 `Ingredient.substance` appears to absorb the main specified-substance identity and strength content, but exact equivalence is uncertain without an official ConceptMap.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Any R4 instance containing `specifiedSubstance` has paths that do not exist in R6. Repeated specified substances may need multiple R6 Ingredient resources or a policy-specific merge. R4 confidentiality appears lossy unless carried by an extension or related artifact.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping confidentiality or merging multiple specified substances incorrectly can change regulated product-disclosure behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Simplify the ingredient model around one substance backbone rather than separate substance and specifiedSubstance branches.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated optional `specifiedSubstance` content or add explicit base R6 fields for its group, confidentiality, and repeated specified-substance semantics.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Simplifying around one R6 substance backbone is a reasonable goal, but the local evidence does not show an adequate base replacement for R4 `specifiedSubstance.group`, `confidentiality`, or multiple specified substances in one resource. Because those fields can be regulatory or disclosure-sensitive, the level of loss and ambiguity is not clearly justified by the supplied artifacts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `specifiedSubstance` as a deprecated optional backbone for transition, or moved its group/confidentiality semantics into explicit optional R6 elements under the new substance model. This is only a partial alternative: retaining the old branch would continue duplicate ways to describe substance identity and strength, and repeated specified substances may conflict with R6's apparent one-Ingredient-per-substance direction.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Improves lossless migration but preserves the old two-branch model and risks duplicate substance representations.

evidence.detail: R4 defines repeating `specifiedSubstance`.
R4 `specifiedSubstance.group` is mandatory 1..1.
R4 provides a confidentiality element under specifiedSubstance.
R6 Ingredient has no `specifiedSubstance` or `confidentiality` element.

examples.examplesMd: The fragment shows R4 content that uses paths absent from R6 `Ingredient`; it is illustrative and omits other required R6 data.

findings.narrativeMd: The R4 resource allowed detailed specified-substance records alongside a simpler substance branch. R6 removes that branch. The main substance code and strengths may map into R6 `Ingredient.substance`, but repeated specified substances, group semantics, and confidentiality require human policy decisions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 `specifiedSubstance` elements are old-valid/new-invalid because R6 has no such element. R6 cannot represent R4 confidentiality without an extension or external policy. If a single R4 resource has multiple specified substances, a one-to-one R6 resource mapping may be invalid or semantically wrong.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory R4 instances with `specifiedSubstance`. For one specified substance, consider mapping its `code` to `Ingredient.substance.code.concept` and its strengths to `Ingredient.substance.strength`. For multiple entries, decide whether to split into multiple R6 Ingredient resources. Preserve `confidentiality` using an agreed extension or related regulated-authorization artifact rather than dropping it silently.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A deprecated retained branch or standard cross-version extension would have made this migration safer. Because R6 omits the branch, implementers must choose between lossy simplification and custom preservation.

findings.title: Strength presentation and concentration fields become choice elements and low-limit fields are removed

oldState.summary: R4 strength uses fixed Ratio fields `presentation` 1..1 and `concentration` 0..1, plus modifier low-limit Ratio fields.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 serializes strength as `presentation`, optional `presentationLowLimit`, optional `concentration`, and optional `concentrationLowLimit`. The low-limit fields are modifier elements indicating a range.

newState.summary: R6 strength uses `presentation[x]` and `concentration[x]` choice elements with Ratio, RatioRange, CodeableConcept, or Quantity; text fields are added.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 serializes the same concepts as choice properties such as `presentationRatio`, `presentationRatioRange`, `presentationCodeableConcept`, `presentationQuantity`, and similarly for concentration. It adds `textPresentation`, `textConcentration`, and `basis`.

facts.newValue: Removed; use RatioRange or other representation
Removed; use RatioRange or other representation

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Definitions for presentation and concentration are similar, but R6 uses FHIR choice-element serialization and absorbs range lower limits into RatioRange.

impact.impactRationaleMd: FHIR choice elements use different JSON property names from the R4 fields. Copying R4 `presentation` to R6 is invalid; it must become `presentationRatio`. R4 low-limit fields have no same-name R6 element. R6 Quantity, CodeableConcept, text-only, or omitted presentations are not cleanly representable in R4, where presentation Ratio was mandatory for each strength.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Strength misinterpretation is high-risk because it can change dose or product-composition meaning.

justification.inferredGoal: Support ranges, textual strengths, and non-ratio strength representations in one strength model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep the old Ratio fields and low-limit fields while adding distinct optional range, quantity, code, and text strength fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 choice/range model is a reasonable way to support RatioRange, Quantity, coded, and text strength representations while removing modifier low-limit fields. A less-breaking additive design exists, but the tradeoffs are material because strength data is clinically sensitive and duplicate representations could diverge.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: R6 could have retained `presentation`, `presentationLowLimit`, `concentration`, and `concentrationLowLimit` and added new fields such as presentation/concentration range, quantity, code, or text variants under distinct names. That would keep R4 Ratio instances valid. It is partial because the same strength could then be represented in old Ratio fields, new range fields, text, or quantity fields, increasing implementation burden and the risk of contradictory dose/composition meaning.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common R4 strength JSON but creates overlapping quantitative representations with safety-sensitive inconsistency risk.

evidence.detail: R4 presentation is 1..1 Ratio.
R4 presentationLowLimit is 0..1 Ratio and isModifier=true.
R6 presentation is a 0..1 choice over Ratio, RatioRange, CodeableConcept, and Quantity.
R6 concentration is a 0..1 choice over Ratio, RatioRange, CodeableConcept, and Quantity.

examples.examplesMd: The RatioRange example is schematic; exact RatioRange element names should be confirmed against the R6 datatype definition during implementation.

findings.narrativeMd: Strength is one of the largest local remodelings. R4 had simple Ratio fields and separate low-limit modifier fields. R6 turns those into choice elements and textual/range-capable representations, which changes both validation and generated accessors.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 strength JSON copied as-is is invalid in R6 because `presentation` is no longer the choice-typed property name and low-limit paths are absent. R6 strength content using Quantity, CodeableConcept, text-only values, or no presentation cannot be losslessly downgraded to R4's mandatory Ratio presentation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map old `presentation` Ratio to `presentationRatio` when no low limit is present. When `presentationLowLimit` is present, consider `presentationRatioRange` after confirming RatioRange structure. Apply the same pattern to concentration. Add tests for plain ratio, range, text, quantity, and missing-presentation cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The choice design is more flexible but breaks common serialized paths. A backward-compatible transition could have kept old Ratio fields as aliases while introducing range/text alternatives, at the cost of duplicate representations.

findings.title: `referenceStrength.substance` becomes required and reference-strength values use choice serialization

oldState.summary: R4 referenceStrength has optional `substance` CodeableConcept, mandatory `strength` Ratio, and optional `strengthLowLimit` Ratio.
oldState.narrativeMd: An R4 reference strength could legally omit the reference substance while still providing a strength Ratio.

newState.summary: R6 referenceStrength requires `substance` CodeableReference and uses `strength[x]` over Ratio, RatioRange, or Quantity.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 requires the relevant reference substance and changes the strength value to choice-element serialization. The old `strengthLowLimit` path is removed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances with reference strength but no reference substance become invalid in R6. Existing R4 `strength` and `strengthLowLimit` fields also need choice/range conversion. R6 Quantity or SubstanceDefinition references cannot always be represented in R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Reference-strength errors can change active-moiety or salt/base equivalence interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Make reference-strength semantics explicit and align strength values with the R6 choice/range model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `referenceStrength.substance` optional in base R6 with a warning or profile requirement, and add richer reference/range forms without replacing the old Ratio shape immediately.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Requiring the reference substance is clinically reasonable because a reference strength without the referenced substance is ambiguous. The less-breaking path is incomplete: it would preserve old incomplete records but would weaken the semantic guarantee R6 appears to be adding, and it would also leave old Ratio and new choice/range representations side by side.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base optional `referenceStrength.substance`, perhaps with an error only in stricter profiles or a warning in the base resource, would preserve R4 reference strengths that omit the substance. Separately, R6 could have added new range/reference fields alongside the old Ratio field. This is partial because it tolerates ambiguous active-moiety/salt-base expressions and duplicate strength encodings in a safety-sensitive area.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Eases migration but allows semantically incomplete reference strengths and overlapping strength encodings.

evidence.detail: R4 `referenceStrength.substance` has cardinality 0..1 and type CodeableConcept.
R6 `referenceStrength.substance` has cardinality 1..1 and type CodeableReference targeting SubstanceDefinition.
R6 reference strength value is a choice over Ratio, RatioRange, and Quantity.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example shows the minimum additional data needed for R6: a reference substance and a choice-typed strength value.

findings.narrativeMd: Reference strength becomes stricter in R6. This is clinically sensible but migration-sensitive because R4 allowed a reference strength without naming the reference substance.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 referenceStrength lacking `substance` can be valid in R4 but invalid in R6. R4 `strength` must be renamed to the correct R6 choice property, and any `strengthLowLimit` must be converted to RatioRange or otherwise preserved.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: For each R4 referenceStrength, populate R6 `substance` from the R4 field if present or derive it from product knowledge before validation. Map `strength` to `strengthRatio`; use `strengthRatioRange` for old low-limit ranges after confirming RatioRange details.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A base required substance avoids ambiguous R6 records, but an incremental migration path could have used a warning invariant first. Systems with historical incomplete data will need backfill or quarantine rules.

findings.title: New `ing-1` invariant constrains allergen use with SubstanceDefinition references

oldState.summary: R4 has `allergenicIndicator` but no local equivalent of `ing-1`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `allergenicIndicator` is a simple optional boolean and R4 substance identity is coded, not a CodeableReference to SubstanceDefinition.

newState.summary: R6 adds invariant `ing-1`: if allergenicIndicator is true, substance should be a code rather than a SubstanceDefinition reference.

constraints.human: If an ingredient is noted as an allergen (allergenicIndicator) then its substance should be a code. If the substance is a SubstanceDefinition, then the allergen information should be documented in that resource

newState.narrativeMd: The constraint prevents representing allergen status on Ingredient when the substance is represented by reference; allergen information should live on the referenced SubstanceDefinition instead.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A straightforward R4 CodeableConcept-to-CodeableReference.concept migration is not affected. A migration that upgrades the substance to a `SubstanceDefinition` reference while retaining `allergenicIndicator=true` will fail R6 validation.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Allergen location affects where safety-sensitive consumers look for allergy information.

justification.inferredGoal: Avoid duplicating allergen statements between Ingredient and SubstanceDefinition.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No R4-preserving base alternative is needed because R4 coded substances can migrate to `CodeableReference.concept` without triggering `ing-1`.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The invariant supports a reasonable single-source-of-truth rule: if a rich `SubstanceDefinition` is referenced, allergen information should live there. This is not a direct R4 instance-preservation problem because R4 has coded substance concepts, and those can migrate as `CodeableReference.concept` while keeping `allergenicIndicator` valid.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A warning-level invariant would be less strict for migrations that choose to normalize old coded substances into `SubstanceDefinition` references while retaining the Ingredient allergen flag. That is a conformance relaxation, not a backward-compatible base-design alternative needed to preserve R4-valid instances. Keeping the error avoids two possible locations for the same allergen assertion when a referenced SubstanceDefinition is available.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Changing the invariant to a warning would ease some enriched migrations but would allow duplicate or conflicting allergen assertions.

evidence.detail: R6 adds local error invariant `ing-1` involving `allergenicIndicator` and `substance.code.reference`.
R4 has allergenicIndicator but no corresponding local invariant.

examples.examplesMd: The invalid example is R6-shaped; it demonstrates the migration pitfall of using a SubstanceDefinition reference while retaining the local allergen flag.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 introduces an error invariant that shifts allergen responsibility when a SubstanceDefinition reference is used. This is a conformance and migration-policy issue more than a direct old-field removal.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 data using coded substances can map to R6 CodeableReference.concept without triggering the invariant. If a mapper chooses CodeableReference.reference for the same data and keeps `allergenicIndicator=true`, R6 validation fails.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When `allergenicIndicator=true`, either keep the substance as a concept on Ingredient or move allergen information into the referenced SubstanceDefinition and omit the Ingredient flag if using a reference. Add validation tests for both concept and reference cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The constraint could have been staged as a warning to ease migration, but the error-level rule enforces a clearer information architecture.

findings.title: R6 adds optional fields with no clear R4 representation

oldState.summary: R4 lacks direct equivalents for R6 `for`, `function`, `comment`, strength text fields, `basis`, and multiple identifiers.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 includes identifier 0..1, role, allergenicIndicator, manufacturer, specifiedSubstance, and substance branches, but not the listed R6 additions.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional product linkage, ingredient function, markdown comment, strength text, basis, and expands identifier to 0..*.
newState.narrativeMd: These additions are generally R4-to-R6 compatible because they are optional or widening, but populated R6 data can be lossy when converted back to R4.

impact.impactRationaleMd: These additions do not make R4 instances invalid in R6 by themselves. They do, however, create backward-conversion and round-trip risks because R4 has no standard fields for the added data or for more than one identifier.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Losing product linkage or ingredient function can affect downstream product composition and regulatory workflows.

justification.inferredGoal: Add expressivity that was missing from the R4 medicinal product ingredient model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: The optional R6 additions and identifier widening already preserve R4-origin instances; the issue is R6-to-R4 export loss, not an R4-to-R6 breaking base design.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional fields is the standard backward-compatible way to evolve a base resource in the forward direction, and widening `identifier` from `0..1` to `0..*` does not invalidate R4 instances. The remaining concern is that R6-native content may be lossy when converted down to R4.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: There is no relevant less-breaking R6 base design for R4-to-R6 compatibility because these fields do not need to be populated for migrated R4 data. R6-to-R4 systems can use extensions or documented loss policies, but those are backward-export mitigations rather than alternatives to the R6 base additions.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Avoiding the additions would preserve backward export fidelity only by forgoing useful R6 expressivity.

evidence.detail: R6 adds product linkage references.
R6 adds ingredient function.
R6 adds markdown comment.
R4 identifier max is 1.
R6 identifier max is *.

examples.examplesMd: This is a valid R6-shaped fragment for the R6-only data-loss pattern; it is not intended to be a complete valid resource.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds useful optional information. Optional additions are not forward-breaking, but they become important when systems must export R6 Ingredient back to R4 or preserve round-trip fidelity.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 validation is not harmed by these optional fields. R6-to-R4 conversion cannot natively carry all values: only one identifier fits R4, and product linkage/function/comment/text/basis need extensions or external mappings.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: When backward conversion is required, define extensions for `for`, `function`, comments, basis, and extra identifiers, or document that they are intentionally dropped. Include round-trip tests for each populated R6-only field.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 additions are mostly appropriate additive evolution. Their reverse-mapping problem is inherent because R4 did not have these fields.

findings.title: R6 adds several terminology bindings that change conformance expectations

oldState.summary: R4 local ingredient elements largely lack terminology bindings in the StructureDefinition.
oldState.narrativeMd: For example, R4 `role`, `specifiedSubstance.group`, substance codes, and country-like strength elements do not declare local bindings in the inspected StructureDefinition.

newState.summary: R6 adds example bindings for role, function, substance codes, and country, plus required bindings for status and manufacturer role.
newState.narrativeMd: `Ingredient.role` is example-bound to `ingredient-role`; `function` to `ingredient-function`; substance CodeableReference concepts to `substance-codes`; countries to `ValueSet/country`. Required bindings apply to `status` and optional `manufacturer.role`.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Most new bindings are example strength and do not by themselves invalidate coded R4 data. Required bindings are attached to new or optional fields already covered by other findings. The practical risk is semantic: applications may begin preferring the R6 code systems and treat legacy local codes as less interoperable.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Terminology differences can affect interoperability but are unlikely to invalidate existing R4 ingredient role codes through the example binding alone.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve terminology guidance for ingredient modeling.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking alternative is needed for the example bindings; required bindings on `status` and optional `manufacturer.role` are covered by their structural findings.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: R6 mostly uses example-strength bindings for role, function, and substance guidance, which does not by itself invalidate legacy codes. The required bindings mentioned in this finding attach to newly added or optional R6 elements addressed elsewhere, so this terminology finding is not an independent R4-to-R6 breaking base-design issue.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The backward-compatible design is effectively what R6 does for the main retained coded concepts: provide example bindings rather than required ones. Systems may map local codes for interoperability, but no base-design alternative is required to preserve R4-valid role or substance codes.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Example bindings improve guidance with minimal validation impact; stronger required bindings on migrated fields would have been more disruptive.

evidence.detail: No R4 binding was present for `role` in the inspected StructureDefinition.
R6 `role` has an example binding to ingredient-role.
The local R6 ingredient-role CodeSystem contains role codes such as Active, Adjuvant, and Excipient.

examples.examplesMd: No hard validation example is included because the primary role/function/substance bindings are example strength. Required status and manufacturer-role effects are covered in separate findings.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 provides more terminology guidance around ingredients. This is not a primary hard break for existing role codes because the key role binding is example strength, but code systems and value-set names may affect UI pick lists, analytics, and conformance documentation.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Example bindings do not require validators to reject codes outside the value set. Required binding validation applies to `status` and to `manufacturer.role` only when that optional role is populated.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Do not recode existing role/function/substance values solely because of example bindings. Consider mapping local codes to R6 ingredient-role and ingredient-function where interoperability is desired, and validate `status`/`manufacturer.role` required bindings explicitly.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Using example bindings is a backward-compatible conformance signal. Stronger required bindings on migrated existing fields would have been much more disruptive.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The R4 Organization manufacturer target is preserved inside R6 `Ingredient.manufacturer.manufacturer`. New R6 references to product definitions and SubstanceDefinition are additive/type-remodeling issues covered in findings; no separate local narrowing of the Organization target was found.
No local fixed, pattern, or default value changes were found on the compared local elements.
No local maxLength, minValue, maxValue, or regex constraints were identified as material changes.
No local slicing or slice-discriminator changes were present in the compared StructureDefinitions.

Most retained clinical fields remain summary elements. Material flag effects are captured where they matter: new modifier `status`, removed modifier low-limit fields, and the manufacturer/status remodelings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: The successor resource is more mature in R6 metadata
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Changing StructureDefinition metadata from R4 draft/trial-use/FMM0 to R6 active/normative/FMM2 does not by itself invalidate instances.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The maturity shift may affect governance, implementation planning, and assumptions about future stability.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: `identifier` widens from 0..1 to 0..*
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is not R4-to-R6 breaking because any single R4 identifier remains valid after mapping.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: R6-to-R4 export is lossy when more than one identifier is present unless extensions or an external identifier-selection rule are used.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional product linkage with `Ingredient.for`
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: `Ingredient.for` is optional, so existing R4 data can migrate without populating it.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Populating `for` can improve R6 graph navigation, but the field has no direct R4 equivalent and may need extensions for backward export.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds optional function and comment fields
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Both fields are optional additions and do not invalidate R4-origin data.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: They are useful places for R6-native detail but should not be silently dropped when converting back to R4.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Ingredient.substance.code` and `referenceStrength.substance` can reference `SubstanceDefinition`; safe migration depends on the target resource's own R4/R6 changes and allergen-data placement.

Inherited constraints and base element changes were intentionally excluded under the assignment scope rule and should be handled by base-artifact reports.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official local ConceptMap or release-note diff was found for `MedicinalProductIngredient` to `Ingredient`, so element matching for `specifiedSubstance` and some semantic fields is inferred from names and definitions.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official HL7 cross-version map or narrative migration note would confirm intended one-to-one, split, or lossy mappings.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparison used local ValueSet and CodeSystem definitions only. No expansion service was used, and SNOMED CT expansion for `substance-codes` was not evaluated.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A terminology server expansion for all bound value sets, plus any official concept maps from local/regulatory code systems, would refine code-level migration risk.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No local example instances for either R4 `MedicinalProductIngredient` or R6 `Ingredient` were found in the package search, so prevalence estimates are based on model structure rather than observed data.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A representative corpus of R4 ingredient instances would quantify how often specified substances, low limits, missing status, and incomplete reference strengths occur.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The report identifies RatioRange as the likely R6 replacement for low-limit strength fields, but did not deeply analyze the RatioRange datatype report because datatype/base-artifact changes are outside this assigned resource scope.
